sections.h: Why walkable Strip apartments are rare
p: The Las Vegas Strip is mostly resorts, casinos and hotel towers rather than apartment buildings. The Strip itself sits just outside city limits in the unincorporated communities of Paradise and Winchester, and the land right around it is mostly resort property. That is why so many locals who work or play on the Strip still drive in every day.
Lura is different. It sits on W Harmon Ave and offers residents direct pedestrian Strip access via the Harmon Bridge, so a night out, a shift or a show can start with a walk.

At Lura you can walk to the Strip over the Harmon Bridge, then come home to resident spaces like the Sky Lounge or pool.

sections.h: Where Strip views come from
p: In Las Vegas, the best known Strip views come from luxury high rises, where floor to ceiling windows and rooftop decks look out over the full length of the Strip. Lower rise buildings can still offer a clear line of sight to the skyline, usually at a lower price than a tower.

There are two kinds of view to ask about: the view from your own home, and the view from shared spaces like a sky lounge or roof deck. A community with a great shared view can give you the Strip at night without paying a premium for a Strip facing home.
Views also shift at night, when the Strip is lit up, so a home that looks ordinary at noon can look very different after dark.

pages.q: Do Las Vegas apartments include utilities?
pages.short: Usually not all of them. Most Las Vegas apartments charge rent plus monthly fees, and you pay usage based costs like electricity on top. At Lura, the posted total monthly price includes base rent and all mandatory monthly fees, but not usage based fees. Ask the leasing team which utilities you set up yourself and what is billed through the community.

sections.h: Why this matters more in Las Vegas
p: Power is the utility to plan for. RentCafe notes that electricity use spikes when temperatures reach 110°F or higher, and suggests asking about typical summer electric bills and whether the cooling system has been updated. A home that looks affordable in spring can feel different in July if the bills surprise you.
It is also worth asking about the history of summer power outages and how quickly management responds to cooling repairs.
